title: SBGR: A Surrogate Bandgap-Reference Benchmark for Constrained Metaheuristic Optimization, with a Transistor-Level SKY130 Cross-Check
description:
Benchmark, optimizers, experiment scripts and campaign data for the study Artificial Bee Colony for Constrained Optimization in 6G-Motivated Analog Integrated Circuit Design: A Surrogate Benchmark and a SKY130 Cross-Check (under review, Applied Soft Computing).

SBGR is a deterministic closed-form benchmark that reproduces the optimization structure of bandgap-reference transistor sizing — maximise power-supply rejection subject to six coupled specifications — for fair, reproducible, simulator-independent comparison of constrained metaheuristics.

Version 1.3 added the transistor-level cross-check: the same constrained-optimization formulation re-posed against bandgap references in the open-source SkyWater SKY130 process and evaluated with ngspice, over five campaigns and 900 runs, 30 paired seed blocks per case. Two campaigns use the current-mode (Banba) core of the motivating reference design, which makes five of its six published specifications applicable verbatim; three use a voltage-mode (Kuijk) core. The measured finding is that an optimizer ranking on this problem is contingent on the specification set, on the core topology and on the evaluator. ABC attains the best average rank and separates from all five baselines under the published specification set; recalibrating the thresholds alone, on the same netlist, the same design box and the same thirty seeds, reverses the ordering and removes the separation; and on the voltage-mode cases the ranking measured on the surrogate does not predict the ranking measured on the circuit. What transfers is reliability rather than peak objective value: ABC reaches a feasible design in every run of every SKY130 case. Separately, of the 540 designs put through a fifteen-condition process-and-supply sweep (8,100 re-simulations) none is verified feasible across all fifteen — 510 of 540 are measured to violate at least one condition, 29 returned no usable measurement and one was measured only in part — and the untouched SKY130 voltage-mode reference design passes 8 of 15 with no solver failure.

Version 1.1 added the two surrogate controls behind Section 6.5 -- SBGR re-run at the circuit's dimensionalities, and with its thresholds relaxed until random in-box feasibility matches the circuit's -- each carrying the published D = 12 cell as a control on the control, which both reproduce exactly. It also adds a direction column to the signed-rank tables, without which five of twenty-five rows read backwards, and a supply-corrected power column to the corner sweeps beside the original one. The only reported numbers this affects are the ones the release itself corrects; the corrections are documented in the README and in results/README_POWER_CORRECTION.md.

This version re-measures the ten current-mode runs affected by a cache-key collision in the evaluator, with the cache disabled, on the machine that ran the campaign. All ten reproduce their recorded infeasibility, so no success rate changes, but each had carried the colliding entry's zero penalty in its recorded fitness. The two campaign files now add cache_collision and best_fitness_remeasured beside the original columns; the paper reports the re-measured value, which moves six average ranks by at most 0.167, three mean-fitness figures, two medians and both current-mode Friedman statistics, and reverses no ordering. Six of the eight derived summary files in each of those two campaign directories, and the fitness boxplots, ship as they ran and are therefore pre-correction; violations.csv and the signed-rank tables are not affected. See results/README_CACHE_CORRECTION.md.

Version 1.4 adds the third round of the transistor-level study: two further circuits pre-registered on 26 August 2026 before either was built — a two-stage operational amplifier and a low-dropout regulator — each run at 150,000 evaluations and, in error, first at 2,500, which are retained as a budget observation. The leader changes again with the topology: ACO on the amplifier (ABC tied for third) and ABC on the regulator, while GWO leads the three voltage-mode bandgap cases and the current-mode leader depends on the threshold set. The per-run records at both budgets, the calibration probes and reference-design searches, and the pre-registration and Circuit B design record (both unedited) are included in this release.

The README documents the exact PDK build and model library with its MD5 checksum, and states ten known issues in the released data, including shipped summary files that should not be used without the corrections recorded beside them.
